title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
description: Defines consumer rights, sets up District, State and National Consumer Commissions, and covers product liability, unfair trade practices and e-commerce.

title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
description: Duties of online marketplaces and sellers, including grievance officers, return and refund policies and display of seller details.

title: Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha (1995)
description: Held that medical services paid for by patients are 'services' under consumer law, so patients can approach Consumer Commissions for medical negligence.

title: Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta (1993)
description: Held that housing construction by a development authority is a 'service' and that compensation can be awarded for harassment and mental agony.

title: Transfer of Property Act, 1882
description: Governs sale, mortgage, lease and gift of immovable property. Chapter V deals with leases, including rights and duties of landlords and tenants.

title: Registration Act, 1908
description: Section 17 makes registration compulsory for sale deeds and for leases of more than one year, which is why many rent agreements are made for 11 months.
keywords: registration, sale deed, rent agreement, lease

title: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
description: Requires registration of real estate projects with state RERA authorities and lets buyers complain about delayed possession or false promises by builders.

title: Model Tenancy Act, 2021
source: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
description: A model law for states that suggests written rent agreements, caps on security deposits and a Rent Authority for quick disputes. It applies only where a state adopts it.

title: Suraj Lamp & Industries v. State of Haryana (2011)
description: Held that property cannot be transferred by a General Power of Attorney or agreement to sell; title passes only through a registered sale deed.
keywords: power of attorney, gpa, sale deed, title

title: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
description: Covers Hindu marriages, grounds for divorce (Section 13), divorce by mutual consent (Section 13B), maintenance and custody.

title: Special Marriage Act, 1954
description: Allows civil marriage between any two persons irrespective of religion, with its own provisions for divorce.

title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
description: Protects women from physical, emotional, sexual and economic abuse at home, and provides protection orders, residence rights and monetary relief.
keywords: domestic violence, abuse, protection order, in-laws

title: Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
description: Makes giving, taking or demanding dowry an offence.

title: Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017)
description: Held that the six-month waiting period for mutual-consent divorce under Section 13B is not mandatory and can be waived by the court in suitable cases.

title: Rajnesh v. Neha (2020)
description: Laid down guidelines on maintenance, including filing affidavits of assets and liabilities and the date from which maintenance is payable.

title: Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017)
description: Declared the practice of instant triple talaq unconstitutional.

title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
description: India's main criminal law, which replaced the Indian Penal Code from 1 July 2024. It defines offences such as theft, cheating, assault and criminal intimidation.

title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
description: Replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure from 1 July 2024. It sets out the procedure for FIRs (including Zero FIR and e-FIR), arrest, bail and trials.

title: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
description: Replaced the Indian Evidence Act from 1 July 2024 and governs what evidence, including electronic records, can be used in court.

title: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh (2013)
description: Held that registration of an FIR is mandatory when information discloses a cognizable offence.

title: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1997)
description: Laid down safeguards to be followed during arrest and detention, such as an arrest memo and informing a relative.

title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014)
description: Directed that police should not arrest automatically for offences punishable with up to 7 years and must record reasons for arrest.

title: Code on Wages, 2019
description: Brings together laws on minimum wages, payment of wages, bonus and equal pay.

title: Industrial Relations Code, 2020
description: Covers trade unions, standing orders, layoffs, retrenchment and resolution of industrial disputes.

title: Code on Social Security, 2020
description: Brings together laws on provident fund, ESI, gratuity and maternity benefit.

title: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
description: Requires employers with 10 or more employees to set up an Internal Committee and provides a complaint process for sexual harassment at work.

title: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997)
description: Recognised sexual harassment at the workplace as a violation of fundamental rights and laid down the guidelines that led to the POSH Act.

title: Information Technology Act, 2000
description: Covers cyber offences such as hacking, identity theft (Section 66C), cheating by impersonation online (Section 66D) and publishing obscene material (Section 67).
keywords: hacking, identity theft, online fraud, obscene

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
description: Sets rules for how organisations collect and use personal data and gives individuals rights over their data.
keywords: data, privacy, data leak, personal data

title: RBI circular on limiting customer liability in unauthorised electronic banking transactions (2017)
description: Limits a customer's liability for unauthorised electronic transactions when they are reported to the bank promptly, generally within three working days.
keywords: bank fraud, upi, card, unauthorised transaction

title: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)
description: Struck down Section 66A of the IT Act for violating freedom of speech.

title: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017)
description: Recognised the right to privacy as a fundamental right under the Constitution.

title: Right to Information Act, 2005
description: Lets citizens request information from public authorities (Section 6), requires a reply within 30 days (Section 7) and provides for appeals (Section 19).

title: CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011)
description: Held that evaluated answer sheets are 'information' and students can inspect them under the RTI Act.

title: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
description: Provides free legal aid through Legal Services Authorities to eligible people, including women, children and low-income persons. NALSA helpline: 15100.
keywords: free legal aid, lawyer, lok adalat
